## Issue

# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api

## Why

`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.

For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.

Raised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.

## What to do

Decide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:

- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.
- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.

Whichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts
- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited
- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing
- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

+# Definition of Done
+
+> `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone. [...] For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere.
+
+**Strategy: `direct`** — The seam exists today: `createChatOrchestrator` takes any `AIProvider`, a scripted provider can report a different `usage` on each round's `stop` chunk, and `hooks.afterModelResponse` receives the third argument. The acceptance tests drive the real tool loop and read what the hook is handed.
+
+Decision recorded for the issue: accumulate across rounds and keep the single `usage` argument (the ticket's first shape). The second shape, passing a per-round breakdown as well, was rejected because the ticket itself requires the no-tool path to report exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing `receives collected response text and usage` test which uses `toEqual` on the bare `UsageMetadata`; extending that object breaks the pin, and a fourth argument widens the public surface for a consumer nobody has named. The acceptance tests assert with `toMatchObject` on the summed fields, so a round that nevertheless adds a breakdown beside the sum (an extra field, or a fourth argument) still passes them.
+
+Spec anchors: this repo exposes no `spec` descriptor field through `.lore/test-commands.yml` (the list command emits id, name and file only), so traceability is carried by the `([validated by: ...])` citations added to `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` under "Usage reported to afterModelResponse".
+
+## Done when these pass
+
+- [ ] **reports 33 input, 13 output and 46 total tokens when three provider calls report 10/5/15, 20/7/27 and 3/1/4** — a turn of two tool rounds (three provider calls) hands `afterModelResponse` the field-by-field sum of every call, not the last call's `3/1/4`
+  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
+- [ ] **reports 15/5/20 when the middle of three calls reports no usage, and nothing when no call reports any** — a call with no `usage` on its stop chunk contributes nothing (no `undefined`, no `NaN`), and a turn where no call reported stays `undefined` rather than becoming zeros
+  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
+- [x] **receives collected response text and usage** (existing, must stay green and unedited) — a turn with no tool calls reports exactly the one call's usage
+  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`
+- [x] **keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none** (existing, must stay green and unedited) — under a sum, a silent later round leaves the earlier round's figures intact
+  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`
+
+## Facets
+
+- [x] Replace the `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` assignment with a pure `addUsage(total, roundUsage)` that sums `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` and `totalTokens` and returns the other operand when one is `undefined`; first acceptance test green

+const stopForTool = (usage?: UsageMetadata): MessageChunk => ({type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_use', usage});
+const stopDone = (usage?: UsageMetadata): MessageChunk => ({type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn', usage});

+async function usageReportedFor(rounds: MessageChunk[][]): Promise<UsageMetadata | undefined> {
+  let reported: UsageMetadata | undefined;

+

+      [TOOL_CALL, stopForTool({inputTokens: 20, outputTokens: 7, totalTokens: 27})],
+      [DONE, stopDone({inputTokens: 3, outputTokens: 1, totalTokens: 4})],

+    expect(reported).toMatchObject({inputTokens: 33, outputTokens: 13, totalTokens: 46});

+        [TOOL_CALL, stopForTool()],
+        [DONE, stopDone({inputTokens: 4, outputTokens: 2, totalTokens: 6})],
+      ]),
+      usageReportedFor([
+        [TOOL_CALL, stopForTool()],
+        [DONE, stopDone()],
+      ]),
+    ]);
+
+    expect({partial, silent}).toMatchObject({
+      partial: {inputTokens: 15, outputTokens: 5, totalTokens: 20},
+      silent: undefined,
+    });
+  });
+});

## The candidate's own definition of done (.lore/dod.md)

# Definition of Done

> `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone. [...] For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere.

**Strategy: `direct`** — The seam exists today: `createChatOrchestrator` takes any `AIProvider`, a scripted provider can report a different `usage` on each round's `stop` chunk, and `hooks.afterModelResponse` receives the third argument. The acceptance tests drive the real tool loop and read what the hook is handed.

Decision recorded for the issue: accumulate across rounds and keep the single `usage` argument (the ticket's first shape). The second shape, passing a per-round breakdown as well, was rejected because the ticket itself requires the no-tool path to report exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing `receives collected response text and usage` test which uses `toEqual` on the bare `UsageMetadata`; extending that object breaks the pin, and a fourth argument widens the public surface for a consumer nobody has named. The acceptance tests assert with `toMatchObject` on the summed fields, so a round that nevertheless adds a breakdown beside the sum (an extra field, or a fourth argument) still passes them.

Spec anchors: this repo exposes no `spec` descriptor field through `.lore/test-commands.yml` (the list command emits id, name and file only), so traceability is carried by the `([validated by: ...])` citations added to `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` under "Usage reported to afterModelResponse".

  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
